items.text: Streaming video platforms have given filmmakers massive budgets and allowed them to make creative and artistic films and series free of the restrictions of cinema or broadcast time slots.

level1.label: 宾语补足语
level1.text: to make creative and artistic films and series free of the restrictions of cinema or broadcast time slots

items.text: But, maybe, just maybe, not everyone wants a three-hour long work of creative genius.

level1.label: 宾语
level1.text: a three-hour long work of creative genius

items.text: Minute-long micro-dramas are taking the entertainment market by storm.
Perhaps most people are looking for something that they can squeeze into their everyday life.

level1.label: 宾语
level1.text: something that they can squeeze into their everyday life

level2.label: 定语从句
level2.text: that they can squeeze into their everyday life

items.text: Micro-dramas cater perfectly for this need.
It's not just that you can watch them on your phone, they're made for it.

level1.label: 表语从句
level1.text: that you can watch them on your phone

items.text: They're shot in vertical format, so you don't even have to turn your phone round to start watching.
Series are split into as many as a hundred short episodes, so they can fit into any spare downtime that you have.
For this to work, it needs a new kind of programme.
US tech company Quibi tried to use traditional Hollywood stars, and collapsed in less than a year, taking $1.75 billion dollars' worth of investment with it.

level1.label: 状语
level1.text: taking $1.75 billion dollars' worth of investment with it

items.text: Chinese start-up companies took a different approach, focusing on low-cost production and using analytics data and AI analysis to identify exactly what gets the audience to start watching, and then how to make the next episode feel unmissable.

level1.label: 状语
level1.text: focusing on low-cost production and using analytics data and AI analysis to identify exactly what gets the audience to start watching, and then how to make the next episode feel unmissable

level2.label: 宾语从句
level2.text: what gets the audience to start watching

level2.label: 宾语从句
level2.text: how to make the next episode feel unmissable

items.text: Billionaires, breakups and bust-ups: those are the key themes that get the audience watching.

level1.label: 表语
level1.text: the key themes that get the audience watching

items.text: There isn't much room for nuance or slow-build character development in a micro-drama, but what is needed is drama.

level1.label: 主语
level1.text: much room for nuance or slow-build character development in a micro-drama

items.text: Rather than a subscription model, monetisation in the world of micro-dramas is often based on a freemium model.

level1.label: 表语
level1.text: often based on a freemium model

items.text: You can see enough episodes to get you hooked for free.

level1.label: 宾语
level1.text: enough episodes to get you hooked

items.text: But you need to buy credits to find out how the story ends.

level1.label: 状语
level1.text: to find out how the story ends

items.text: This means that dramatic cliffhangers are a commercial tool.

level1.label: 宾语从句
level1.text: that dramatic cliffhangers are a commercial tool

items.text: These dramas are increasing in popularity around the world.
There is also great potential to make money from advertising as audiences are highly engaged.

level1.label: 主语
level1.text: great potential to make money from advertising

items.text: After China, the US has become the biggest micro-drama market.
Could it be that soon most of the drama we watch is on our phones in those minutes we find between our other daily tasks?

level1.label: 表语从句
level1.text: that soon most of the drama we watch is on our phones in those minutes we find between our other daily tasks

level2.label: 定语从句
level2.text: we find between our other daily tasks
